transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-15 09:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Samira Gomez (Redwood CSM); Martin Chen (CTO), Aisha Rahman (ML Eng), Diego Morales (DevOps), Nora Li (Product)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Helix is evaluating Redwood for inference; key reqs: multi-lingual, long context for legal docs (up to 64k), tool calling to integrate booking and internal search, want options for Hosted first then Dedicated/Private for regulated data.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I'm Jordan with Redwood, this is Priya on the SE side and Samira who runs a lot of our onboarding. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Martin Chen: Good thanks, Martin here. We got a bunch of people from eng and product, appreciate the time.
[00:11] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Quick agenda — a few discovery q's about your workloads, then model and deployment tradeoffs, and then next steps / POC scoping. Sound ok?
[00:17] Aisha Rahman: Yep sounds great. We've been evaluating open models, we've tried a few locally and also tested Anthropic and OpenAI via API. Main things for us — multilingual, ability to pass in long legal documents (sometimes 30-60k tokens), and we need tool-calling for our booking and document retrieval APIs.
[00:33] Priya Patel: Thanks Aisha — couple clarifying q's: what languages are important and what's the latency SLO you're targeting for interactive flows?
[00:40] Aisha Rahman: Primary languages are English, Spanish, Portuguese, and occasionally French/Japanese for support. Latency target for chat flows is under 500ms p95 for short prompts; for long document QA we can tolerate a few seconds but want predictable performance.
[00:54] Diego Morales: And around data residency — some documents are PII/PHI, so eventually we'll likely want VPC or on-prem options. For now, though, we want to prototype on Hosted if that's feasible.
[01:03] Jordan Lee: Totally makes sense, Helix pattern we see a lot — Hosted for quick iteration then Dedicated or Private for compliance. For model selection, are you leaning toward a specific open model family?
[01:13] Martin Chen: We've seen good quality from Mistral in benchmarks and some Llama-2 forks at scale, but the long-context variants are more interesting — 32k vs 64k context. We're also curious about Redwood's verified model catalog and any perf/quantization tradeoffs.
[01:26] Priya Patel: Right — Redwood maintains performance profiles for models. For 64k workflows we recommend models that have native long context or have been tiled/extended; there are tradeoffs in latency and memory. Also worth discussing prefix/KV caching and chunked retrieval to reduce repeated token cost.
[01:39] Nora Li: On tool-calling — we need structured outputs (JSON) back to call our booking API and a safe sandbox for tool execution. Does Redwood support function/tool calls with policy controls?
[01:49] Priya Patel: Yes — hosted and dedicated support function-calling / tool-calling. We also have structured output enforcement and ability to gate which tools are available per model/route. For Private on-prem we provide the runtime and hooks, but tool execution must be hosted within customer's network for security.
[02:03] Aisha Rahman: Great. For multilingual quality — do you have recommended models that are particularly strong outside English? The ones we tried dropped in Spanish legal terms.
[02:12] Priya Patel: Mistral-variant and some community Llama-3 forks have good multilingual tokenizers and pretraining. Redwood's catalog flags models with stronger multilingual evals. Keep in mind quantization can slightly impact non-English tokenization quality, so we usually recommend running a small multilingual pass during POC.
[02:28] Diego Morales: On cost — can you outline expected token cost delta between Hosted & Dedicated? Also how does batching and autoscaling affect our per-token pricing?
[02:36] Jordan Lee: Short answer: Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated gives committed capacity and lower per-token CPU/GPU unit cost but requires monthly commit. Batching, caching and KV reuse improve unit economics significantly — Redwood Optimize suggestions can tune the batch sizes and caching to meet latency SLOs while lowering cost. We'll send a TCO spreadsheet with examples.
[02:52] Martin Chen: Any differences in latency for tool-calls when hosted vs dedicated?
[02:56] Priya Patel: Dedicated typically has slightly better tail latency because you have reserved GPU pools — fewer noisy neighbors. Hosted has auto-scaling but might hit warmup for cold models; we mitigate that with model variants and pre-warmed nodes for enterprise customers.
[03:10] Aisha Rahman: We also need audit logs, KMS integration for key management, and SSO (SAML) for the console. How mature are those features?
[03:17] Samira Gomez: We support SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can opt into KMS for encryption at rest and we have SOC2 docs to share. For on-prem we support HSM workflows in the private control plane.
[03:31] Martin Chen: Good. One technical item — we're concerned about memory blow-up with 64k context on standard A100s. Does Redwood recommend specific hardware or sharding patterns?
[03:39] Priya Patel: For 64k we often recommend larger memory instances or multi-node serving with KV cache streaming. Our runtime supports continuous KV cache and attention kernel selection; in practice some customers use quantized 8-bit kernels with memory optimized operators on H100/A100 80GB variants or multi-GPU serving. We'll include recommended instance types in the doc.
[03:56] Diego Morales: For the POC, can Redwood provide a benchmark harness or should we bring our own?
[04:00] Priya Patel: We'll provide a sample harness and baseline results for the models you select; we prefer customers to run their prompts too so results reflect your distribution. We'll include multilingual and 64k test sets in the template.
[04:10] Martin Chen: Ok timeline — we'd like to have a POC scope and cost by next week and start a 2-week pilot after sign-off. Security review may require a separate call with our compliance folks.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: Sounds good — we'll send the pricing/TCO and SOC2 docs and schedule the POC scoping. Priya, can you take point on benchmarks?
[04:25] Priya Patel: Yep I'll put together the benchmark template and sample prompts; also include a checklist for tool-call sandboxing, API rate limits, and tokenization caveats for non-English languages.
[04:35] Nora Li: One more question — do you support incremental rollout and canarying between model variants? We want to try cheaper quantized variants but fall back to higher-quality ones if regression happens.
[04:44] Priya Patel: Yes — Redwood Console supports rollout policies, canary and A/B test routing, automatic fallback to a pinned variant if quality drops. We can tie regressions to evals and prompt sets so we get alerts.
[04:56] Aisha Rahman: That is useful. Also, can we keep a hot prefix cache for legal templates so repeated queries are faster and cheaper?
[05:02] Priya Patel: Absolutely — prefix/KV caching is supported and we can scope cache eviction policies by route or tenant. That helps with both latency and cost.
[05:12] Martin Chen: Ok wrapping up. Quick recap of next steps please?
[05:15] Jordan Lee: Jordan: send pricing + TCO spreadsheet and SOC2 docs tomorrow. Priya: benchmark template and sample prompts by Thursday. Diego: share infra histogram. Martin: confirm security reviewer availability. We'll put a POC scoping call on calendar for 2026-03-22.
[05:31] Diego Morales: Sounds good. Thanks team.
[05:34] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links and docs.

(Transcript notes — some words mistranscribed by auto system; proper nouns sometimes garbled: e.g., Mistral variants or model forks may appear slightly different in auto text.)

End of call.

Post-call recap (auto): Redwood to provide pricing, SOC2/ISO docs, benchmark harness + template for multilingual and 64k context tests; customer to provide infra distribution and security contacts. Proposed POC week of 3/29 pending scoping.
